still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has still approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US, and generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there. Maintenance still costs $299.
The 503B compounding exclusion finalised in 2026 still stands, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels.
Illinois's 2028 ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still in force, and the September 2027 tri-agency guidance still allows wellness differentials of up to 30% in every other state.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 28.5% ever-used minus 21.5% current = 7.0 points of adults (~18.8M of ~268M) who have used the drugs and are off them now. 45% of ever-users have cycled, which is 12.8 points: about 10.8 points are current users on at least their second course (50% of current users), and 2.0 points cycled before and are off again. That fits roughly one-third persistence at one year and 36–47% restarting within a year, applied to a larger and older base. More restarts now run through scheduled 'drug holidays' rather than lapses. 21.5% of ~268M is ~57.6M current users. Payer mix: Medicare ~15.5M (26.9%), Medicaid ~6.5M (11.3%), commercial ~13.5M (23.4%), legitimate cash ~18.6M (32.3%), gray market ~3.5M (6.1%), for a total of 57.6M. Public payers cover ~22M (38%), the largest single payer category, and the default for 65+ and low-income users. The 65+ band rose from 12% to 22% (~13.6M of ~62M), driven by the January 2030 Medicare obesity benefit and the dementia and AUD codes. Age-band check: 0.20×11 + 0.33×21 + 0.24×31 + 0.23×22 ≈ 21.6. The bottom income third rose from 11% to 18% on Medicaid opt-ins and Medicare-eligible low-income seniors, but still trails the top. Adult obesity is ~33.4%. About 20% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug: mostly working-age uninsured people, people on Medicaid in the 23 non-covering states, and deliberate refusers. Under-18 use rose only slightly, from 0.8% to 0.9%, because state minors' laws slowed adolescent starts. About 0.4M adolescents remain on a drug, concentrated in upper-income households in states without age floors.

access.public_coverage: The Medicare Metabolic Health Act (signed Jul 2029, effective Jan 2030) covers incretins under Part D for BMI ≥35, or ≥30 with a comorbidity. The copay is $50 and the manufacturer net price is locked at $245 through 2033. Medicare already covered users under cardiovascular, kidney, sleep-apnoea, diabetes and dementia codes (~9.3M), plus ~1.2M under AUD codes, which are outside the statutory weight-loss exclusion. The new benefit added ~5.0M in its first year, for ~15.5M total. Arithmetic: 15.5M × $245 × 12 ≈ $45.6B gross a year. Beneficiary copays are 15.5M × $50 × 12 ≈ $9.3B, leaving ~$36.3B a year for Medicare. The new benefit alone costs 5.0M × $195 × 12 ≈ $11.7B a year. CBO scored the Act at ~$96B over 2030–2039, assuming an average 4.1M enrollees × $195 × 12 ≈ $9.6B a year. First-year enrolment is already ~20% above that average, and CBO has flagged a re-estimate. The Act also lets states cover incretins in Medicaid at the $245 rate at the regular match. 27 states now do, covering ~6.5M people: 6.5M × $245 × 12 ≈ $19.1B a year, about two-thirds federal (~$12.7B).
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide costs $6–40 a month across 80+ brands, and Chinese makers supply most API outside the US. Generic tirzepatide is not yet approved anywhere major. Canadian generic semaglutide is CAD 70–110. Prices outside the US have stopped falling as API consolidates and Gulf and Latin American demand absorbs capacity.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices stalled. Wegovy's list price is still $1,349. TrumpRx cash prices are unchanged since 2028: oral Wegovy is $149 to start and $299 for maintenance, Foundayo is $149–349, and injectables are $299–449. The Medicare $245 is a ceiling written into law, not a starting point. Retatrutide (approved Apr 2029) launched at a ~$1,250 list and ~$599–699 cash. Bimagrumab adjunct (approved Feb 2030) is ~$1,100 a month on list, and supply allocation limits who can get it. Employer coverage for weight management fell from 44% to 41%. Many employers now carve out Medicare-eligible retirees and push them to the public benefit. Under federal mental-health parity, plans that dropped weight coverage must still cover AUD indications, so 'coding drift' toward AUD diagnoses is a recognised audit issue. Orals are ~64% of new starts and ~51% of all users. The gray market shrank in share (7% → 6%) but grew slightly in absolute terms, to ~3.5M people. It is mostly working-age adults in non-covering Medicaid states and people seeking adolescent or microdose supply that state laws now restrict.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Apr 2029)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, approved Sep 2029 for obesity with MASH)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus; AUD indication Jun 2030)
Activin type II receptor antibody, 4-weekly subcutaneous, muscle-preserving adjunct to incretin therapy (bimagrumab, Lilly, approved Feb 2030)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established cardiovascular disease (tirzepatide; confirmatory trial ongoing)
moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder in adults (oral semaglutide, Jun 2030; ASAM guideline conditional recommendation, Oct 2029)
knee osteoarthritis pain in adults with obesity (retatrutide)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: AUD with injectables and Foundayo, ahead of their own labels
dementia prevention in 55–75-year-olds without cardiovascular disease
microdosing for 'evenness', now often in pulsed weekday-only schedules
nicotine and gambling reduction; a phase 3 smoking-cessation trial is under way
scheduled 'drug holidays' of 3–14 days around holidays, travel and anniversaries, sometimes recommended by clinicians to manage blunting
bimagrumab use by under-60s without sarcopenia risk to 'protect muscle' during weight loss (cash, where supply allows)
drugs.pipeline_note: The muscle-preserving-combo driver is realised by Lilly's bimagrumab. Lilly filed the BLA in Jan 2029 on a phase 2b/3 trial showing about half the lean-mass loss with tirzepatide and similar total weight loss. The FDA approved it in Feb 2030 as an adjunct for adults 60+ or with documented low lean mass. It is marketed as a co-pack with Zepbound. No fracture-outcome data exist; a postmarketing fracture trial is required. Muscle preservation is shown on DXA, not on hips, but the 'skinny-frail problem solved' framing is everywhere in ads that can still run. Biologic fill-finish capacity limits supply to about 0.6M patients. Retatrutide was approved in Apr 2029 after its extended review, with a dysesthesia warning and ~27% mean weight loss at the top dose. Survodutide (Boehringer) was approved in Sep 2029 for obesity with MASH, making Boehringer the first branded incretin seller other than Novo and Lilly. The oral semaglutide AUD sNDA was filed in Mar 2029 and approved in Jun 2030. Amycretin was filed in May 2029 and its decision is due in 2031 after a major amendment. MariTide's BLA was filed in Apr 2030 and it is not on the market. No oral matches tirzepatide. The global incretin market is ~$150B (2030), and US net prices are flat.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Retatrutide has higher early GI rates at the top dose.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; more cases at triple-agonist magnitudes of loss.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. The 2028 hip-fracture HR of ~1.3 in users aged 65+ held in a 2029 replication. It is now applied to a Medicare user base that has roughly doubled. The bimagrumab adjunct halves lean-mass loss on DXA in trials, but no fracture data exist. Fewer than 5% of users aged 65+ are on it because of supply and prior authorisation.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The class warning from Jul 2028 stands. The Medicare Act requires a baseline DXA for new beneficiaries 70+, and protein counselling is a billable code. The bimagrumab label states fracture benefit is not established.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed as an adverse reaction; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal, including in the AUD trial population.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. An interim analysis of the FDA-requested postmarketing study (2030, n≈61k) found a clinically meaningful anhedonia increase in ~6–8% of users versus ~3% of controls. It is dose-related and reverses partly within 2–4 weeks of dose reduction or a holiday. It is higher with retatrutide. In the AUD population, lower reward from alcohol is the intended effect.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelling negotiation under way; the FDA has signalled an adverse-reactions entry, not a boxed warning. The AUD label includes mood-monitoring language.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Short drug holidays of under 2 weeks show little regain.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; supports chronic-therapy framing in the Medicare Act.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiencies persist, especially among older Medicare enrollees eating very little.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; the Medicare Act funds annual lab panels for enrollees.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects in adolescents; effects of repeated cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About eight years of adult follow-up exists. There are still no adolescent peak-bone-mass outcome data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone-density postmarketing requirement; state age-floor laws (see state).

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Adverse-event reports have slowed as public coverage absorbed some gray-market users. Mg/unit dosing errors remain the main issue. One more contaminated-lot cluster (2029, 9 hospitalisations).
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alert and CBP seizures continue. US–India enforcement memorandum (2029) covers mail-order exporters.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-duration rebound hyperphagia ('lock-in'): appetite above pre-treatment baseline after stopping following 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL, novel long-horizon signal. A Danish national registry study linked to Kaiser Permanente data (Mar 2030, n≈38k who stopped after ≥5 years of continuous semaglutide use) found 18-month regain averaging ~115% of weight lost, versus ~60% in people stopping after under 2 years. Validated hunger scores were above their own pre-treatment baselines in ~30% at 12 months. Small fMRI and hormone substudies suggest lasting hypothalamic adaptation. It was not seen in trials, which never ran past ~4 years. It is not dangerous in itself, but it makes stopping after long use much harder, and it falls on the earliest and oldest users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (Apr 2030), with label language under discussion. EMA PRAC review opened. Endocrine Society statement advising clinicians to discuss 'exit planning' before year five. No restriction on continued use.

food_and_beverage.state: About 38% of US households now have a user, and a growing share are older households on the Medicare benefit. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~7–9% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~7%. Price increases and smaller packs keep dollar sales roughly flat to slightly down. Shelf-stable protein and 'senior nutrition' lines (Ensure-type, protein puddings) are the growth aisle, helped by Medicare protein counselling. Volume pressure has spread from middle-income suburbs to retirement-heavy Sun Belt metros: Phoenix, Tampa, The Villages.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~11% from 2025 and beer ~7%. The AUD approval and parity-driven coverage put the drug into the hands of the heaviest-drinking 10% who buy most volume. Brown-Forman and Diageo have closed more US capacity, and mid-tier American whiskey has a supply glut. Non-alcoholic and 'one-pour' premium lines grow, and bars in Milwaukee, Louisville and Pittsburgh are consolidating.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat and checks are slightly lower. Small plates, protein add-ons and 'half-portion' pricing are standard. Early-dinner senior traffic is weaker in Florida and Arizona. Bar-adjacent casual dining (wings, sports bars) is the weakest segment. Dessert attach rates are still falling.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists are smaller, but the decline has slowed as regainers and refusers form a stable market. Mainstream retailers are adapted to size-cycling with stretch fits and adjustable waistbands. Senior apparel sees a resizing wave like the one younger shoppers went through in 2026–27.

fitness.state: Strength training, physical-therapy-gym hybrids and DXA chains are growing. Medicare Advantage plans bundle resistance-training benefits with the obesity benefit. The 'lean-mass protection' framing has moved partly from gyms to the bimagrumab co-pack, and some studios report under-60 members dropping lifting in favour of 'the muscle shot'.

insurance.state: Employer coverage for weight management fell to 41%. Employers are shifting Medicare-eligible retirees and older workers to the public benefit. Pharmacy trend has moderated to ~+7% as some cost moves to Medicare. AUD parity obligations have created a coverage backdoor and audits of AUD coding. Adherence-premium programmes persist outside Illinois and California but now build in 'holiday allowances' after the EEOC conciliation. Medicare Part D premiums rose ~8% for 2030, partly attributed to the obesity benefit.

pharma.state: Lilly leads on efficacy with retatrutide and owns the only muscle adjunct. Novo leads on orals and now AUD. Boehringer is a small third entrant. US net prices are flat. Volume growth is driven by Medicare, and the $245 locked price gives a predictable floor. Bimagrumab supply is constrained. Ex-US generic prices are flat.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: A lean body over 50 signals nothing in particular now. A visibly heavy body over 65 prompts the question 'are you not eligible?' Someone regaining fast after years on the drug is read, since the April lock-in story, as someone who 'stopped too late' rather than someone who lost coverage.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The class gradient has narrowed at the bottom and changed shape at the top. Medicare and Medicaid made the drug ordinary for the poor and old. The upper tier is now marked by what it adds: retatrutide, the bimagrumab co-pack, DXA every six months, a clinician who plans holidays and an 'exit'. The never-treated are concentrated among working-age uninsured adults in Texas, Florida and Georgia, which have not opted in to Medicaid coverage.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: In retirement communities like The Villages, Florida, potlucks have become 'protein tables' and early-bird specials are shrinking. Family holidays are planned around who is on a holiday from the drug that week. The Tulsa 'Bread Alone' fast network claims ~500 congregations but reads now as an alternative practice, not a protest.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profile tags for 'on' or 'off' have faded on mainstream apps because 'on' is assumed. 'Holidaying' is the new disclosure: people schedule first dates and anniversaries during drug holidays to 'feel it fully'. Couples therapists say desire mismatch now presents more as timing than as a split between on and off.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Normalisation. For most adults over 40, taking it is like taking a statin, and not taking it, or stopping, needs an explanation: side effects, coverage, refusal. The lock-in finding added a new moral reading of appetite as something to be preserved, prompting 'exit planning' conversations. The Unmuted collective has turned from protest into a scene with a following.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Measured meaningful anhedonia in ~6–8% of users versus ~3% of controls (2030 interim postmarketing data). Far more users, perhaps a third in surveys, describe a milder flatness they now name and manage. Dose reduction and holidays of 3–14 days are common. Clinicians estimate ~25% of current users take a scheduled holiday at least twice a year.
interior_life.framing: A side effect everyone knows about, like statin muscle aches. 'Being flat' is ordinary talk. HR has quietly dropped 'steadiness' from benefit decks. Pharma calls it 'tolerability' and sells lower maintenance doses. In the AUD clinic it is the treatment itself.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Adherence-verified programmes still cover ~3.4M employees, but after the 2029 EEOC conciliation with a Texas logistics firm and California's ban (effective 2030), most allow two documented holidays a year without premium penalty. Managers joke about 'holiday week' productivity. Commercial drivers on AUD indications are now a DOT question; FMCSA opened a guidance docket in 2030. Sales and creative firms report people asking to lower their dose for pitches.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Unmuted 'off nights' in Philadelphia and Brooklyn have been copied by Austin and Minneapolis venues as 'holiday shows'. The 'flat fiction' wave has become a recognised genre, with an awards category at one indie prize. Sportsbook handle growth has slowed. Late-night bar culture keeps shrinking in mid-sized cities, while daytime venues and hot-sauce culture keep growing.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples schedule holidays together. Reproductive endocrinologists see more couples coming off for conception and struggling with regain. Some partners of long-term users describe the lock-in news as 'learning my husband can't stop'.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Coalition politics over coverage and kids, not mood. The Medicare Act passed with large bipartisan margins on senior demand. The restriction push (minors, advertising) unites MAHA-aligned legislators, pediatricians and parents' groups. Fat-acceptance groups split over the minors' laws. There is still no measurable turnout or mood effect, and 'sedated electorate' claims remain unsupported.

state.regulatory_posture: Expansive on coverage and approvals, restrictive on promotion and minors. The FDA approved retatrutide, survodutide, bimagrumab and the AUD indication within 15 months. In Nov 2029 it rescinded the 'adequate provision' standard for broadcast ads of incretin and other chronic-therapy drugs, which in practice took incretin TV ads off the air. A companion FTC/FDA policy on paid-influencer telehealth promotion led to ~40 warning letters.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The Medicare Metabolic Health Act (2029) makes Part D the default payer for older adults: $245 locked net price, $50 copay, chronic-therapy framing. The Medicaid option is taken up by 27 states. There is no mandate to use the drug.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: PBM fill-verification continues under the 2027 guidance, softened by holiday allowances and banned in Illinois and California. Medicare requires DXA for enrollees 70+ and annual labs, but no adherence conditions. Two state Medicaid programmes still tie continuation to BMI progress, and one is in litigation.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE has broadened coverage to AUD codes, and the Army expanded supervised oral use for recruits. FMCSA has opened a docket on commercial drivers taking incretins for AUD. Several trucking firms now require disclosure.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China remain the world's volume source. The 2029 US–India enforcement memorandum covers mail-order exporters in exchange for tariff relief on other generics. Bimagrumab biologic capacity, concentrated in Lilly plants in Indiana and Ireland, is the new bottleneck. Danish politics now features the lock-in registry finding, since Denmark has the longest-treated population.

events.event: Medicare Metabolic Health Act signed: from January 2030, Part D covers incretins for obesity at a $50 copay. Lilly and Novo lock the net price at $245 through 2033. CBO scores it at $96B over ten years, and states may add Medicaid coverage at the same rate.

FDA rescinds the 'adequate provision' standard for broadcast drug ads, driving incretin commercials off TV. Eleven states, including Texas, Utah and Tennessee, have now set an age-16 floor for weight-loss incretins, with pediatric-specialist and baseline-DXA requirements for 16–17-year-olds.

EEOC reaches conciliation with a Texas logistics firm over premium penalties for employees who paused GLP-1s for side effects. Large employers add 'holiday allowances' to adherence programmes as California's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums takes effect.

FDA approves Lilly's bimagrumab as a muscle-preserving adjunct to tirzepatide for adults 60+ or with low lean mass. DXA data show half the lean-mass loss; no fracture data. Lilly allocates supply as demand exceeds fill-finish capacity.

Danish registry and Kaiser study finds people who stop semaglutide after five or more continuous years regain more weight than they lost, with hunger above their own pre-treatment baselines. FDA issues a Drug Safety Communication and the EMA opens a review.

FDA approves oral semaglutide for moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder, months after ASAM's conditional endorsement. Under federal parity rules, employer plans that dropped weight coverage must still cover the AUD indication.

open_tensions: Medicare is now the default payer for a therapy that a new long-horizon signal suggests is hard to leave after five years. CBO's 4.1M-enrollee average is already exceeded in year one, and the $245 price lock runs only to 2033.

The muscle problem is 'solved' in ads and DXA scans but not in hip fractures. The supply-limited bimagrumab adjunct goes mostly to the cash-rich, while the oldest and frailest Medicare enrollees take incretins without it.

Drug holidays have become the accepted fix for blunting. But they are a form of the cycling that drives regain and fat-over-muscle recovery, and employer adherence programmes still pay people not to take them beyond two a year.

State age floors cover 11 states. Elsewhere, upper-income adolescents keep starting through the years when peak bone mass forms. In restricted states, families turn to out-of-state telehealth and the gray market, which the minors' laws cannot reach.

prose.headline: Medicare Now Pays for Your Appetite. The Hard Part, a New Study Says, Is Giving It Back
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2030 a little more than one American adult in five is taking an incretin drug, and nearly three in ten have tried one. For a growing number, the government is paying. In July 2029 Congress did what it had refused to do two years earlier. With older voters still angry about the lapsed Bridge pilot and a dementia label on tirzepatide, it passed the Medicare Metabolic Health Act. Since January, a beneficiary with obesity pays $50 a month for a drug whose net price Lilly and Novo have locked at $245. In return the companies got predictability. About fifteen million Medicare enrollees now take one of these drugs, and twenty-seven states have used the same deal to add them to Medicaid. Public programmes are now the largest payer. CBO scored the law at ninety-six billion dollars over ten years. First-year enrolment already exceeds its ten-year average.

Prices did not fall. Wegovy's list price is still $1,349. The government cash channel still sells starting pills for $149 and maintenance for $299, as it did two years ago. Retatrutide arrived in April 2029 and does more than anything before it, at a higher price. Lilly's bimagrumab, approved in February, is the first drug sold to stop the muscle loss, and there is not enough of it. Its DXA scans look good. Nobody yet knows whether it prevents broken hips, and the label says so. The advertising says that problem is handled. Not much advertising remains, though. Since November, broadcast ads have had to recite their full risks, so incretin commercials have left television.

Being on the drug has become unremarkable. In The Villages, Florida, potlucks have turned into protein tables. Being off it is what people ask about now: side effects, a coverage gap, principle. The question got harder in April, when a Danish and Kaiser study of people who stopped after five or more continuous years found they regained more than they had lost. Some reported hunger above where they started. Nobody is in danger. But the earliest and most faithful users have learned that the exit may be narrower than the entrance, and endocrinologists have started talking about exit planning before year five.

The flatness has a name everyone uses. Six to eight percent of users show measurable loss of pleasure, and many more describe something milder. They manage it the way statin users manage aches: lower doses, and holidays of a few days to two weeks around weddings, anniversaries and pitches. Employers that sold 'steadiness' have stopped saying the word. After an EEOC settlement and California's ban, most adherence programmes allow two holidays a year without a premium penalty. Weight researchers note that a holiday is a short version of the cycling that rebuilds fat faster than muscle.

In June the FDA approved oral semaglutide for alcohol use disorder. Federal parity law means employer plans that dropped weight coverage must still pay for it, and AUD coding has become something auditors watch. Spirits volume is down about eleven percent from 2025. Bars in Milwaukee and Louisville are closing or merging, and the trucking industry is waiting to hear whether a driver on an AUD prescription needs to tell anyone.

Children are the one place the state pulled back. Eleven states now bar weight-loss incretins for anyone under sixteen and require specialists and bone scans after that. Elsewhere, upper-income teenagers keep starting. In the restricted states some families find an out-of-state telehealth doctor or a vial in the mail. On the surface the country is thinner, drinks less, and has more older people in strength-training classes than ever. Much of that is real. Underneath, millions of Americans have started a treatment that is getting harder to stop.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Vega turns sixty-seven on a Tuesday in San Antonio and spends the morning at a DXA clinic in a former Pier 1. The technician tells her to lie still and think of nothing. She thinks of cake.

The Wegovy pill sits in her purse in its blister pack, thirty a month, fifty dollars at the H-E-B pharmacy since January. She has decided to skip it today and tomorrow. Dr. Patel calls that a holiday. Her granddaughter calls it 'going loud.'

The scan shows her hips down two percent. The clinic's tablet offers her a pamphlet about the muscle shot. In small type at the bottom: availability limited, prior authorization required. She folds it into quarters.

At lunch her husband Ernesto orders the half-portion enchiladas and eats all of them. Ernesto took Ozempic for his sugar for seven years and stopped last spring when his stomach turned. Now he is hungry in a way she has never seen, like a teenager. He read the Danish study on his phone and told her, 'Seven years, Mari. I'm one of the ones.' He is not angry about it. He orders sopapillas.

At four her grandson Diego, fifteen, comes over to mow. He asked his mother for the pill last summer, and the state said no until he's sixteen. A boy at school gets vials from somewhere. Diego says he doesn't want them. Marisol believes him about half.

That night the family eats tres leches on the patio. Marisol has two slices and tastes every one of them. She thinks it may be the best thing that happened all year. On Thursday she takes a pill again.

least_plausible_claims.quote: plus ~1.2M under AUD codes, which are outside the statutory weight-loss exclusion
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: Medicare is said to cover about 1.2M people for AUD when the January 2030 benefit starts, but the FDA only approved the AUD indication in Jun 2030. The candidate shows no compendia listing or other route for Part D to cover an off-label use at that scale, so the figure looks asserted to inflate the Medicare total.

least_plausible_claims.quote: found 18-month regain averaging ~115% of weight lost, versus ~60% in people stopping after under 2 years.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude and mechanism: a 38k-person registry cohort of people who stopped after 5+ years of continuous use is large for 2030, since few patients are that adherent. Regain exceeding total weight lost within 18 months is far above the 50–67% baseline, and the hypothalamic-adaptation mechanism rests on small substudies.

Mechanism: opt-in states roughly triple from about 9 in 2028 (14 minus 5 dropouts) to 27, even though the starting world says Medicaid budgets were under pressure. The candidate gives no reason states would take on a ~$6B state share, because the Act's $245 rate and 'regular match' is not shown to differ from what was already on offer.

rationale.badness: Coverage reaches poorer and older people, so the class gradient narrows, and the harms are measured and openly discussed (anhedonia at 6–8%, a Drug Safety Communication on lock-in, DXA requirements). Real losses remain. About 13.6M people 65+ are on a class with an unresolved hip-fracture signal. A new lock-in problem falls on the earliest and oldest users. Adherence-conditioned premiums persist outside Illinois and California, and adolescents in states without age floors keep starting. That makes a harder society with new losers, not a structurally hidden one.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible in fields and events, including the stalled price path (list and cash prices unchanged, net prices flat), the Medicare Act, oral semaglutide for AUD, the lock-in signal, bimagrumab, normalisation, age floors and ad rescission, and the mainstream-complaint framing. mechanism: the main chains are shown (Bridge lapse and dementia label leading to the Act, parity leading to AUD coding drift, EEOC leading to holiday allowances). The weak points are Medicare AUD users counted before the Jun 2030 approval, the tripling of Medicaid states without a stated reason, and the extreme lock-in magnitudes (claims 1–3). magnitude: population figures sit inside the envelope (21.5%, 28.5%), and payer mix, age bands, income thirds and the CBO and Medicare arithmetic all reconcile. Approval timings obey the rules. Small gaps remain: the Medicare spend ignores retatrutide and bimagrumab prices, 'contained' gray market conflicts with its absolute growth, and 0.4M adolescents sits oddly against 0.9% of under-18s.
rationale.generativity: The Marisol Vega vignette is concrete: a DXA clinic in a former Pier 1, a pill holiday, Ernesto's post-stop hunger, Diego and the vials, and tres leches. The world has many filmable locales (The Villages protein tables, holiday shows, the FMCSA docket, 'holidaying' dates). Texture is strong, though the vignette explains the Danish study somewhat.

least_plausible_claims.quote: found 18-month regain averaging ~115% of weight lost, versus ~60% in people stopping after under 2 years.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: regain above 100% of weight lost within 18 months is extreme for a registry cohort. Long-term users who stop are self-selected (for example, Ernesto stopped because of GI symptoms), and the cohort sits at the edge of any trial data, so the confounding is large. The 'lasting hypothalamic adaptation' explanation is asserted from small substudies.

least_plausible_claims.quote: About 0.4M adolescents remain on a drug, concentrated in upper-income households in states without age floors.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: 0.9% of roughly 73M under-18s is about 0.65M, not 0.4M. The 2028 baseline of 0.8% is also about 0.58M, so the figure fails to reconcile. The prose case (a Texas 15-year-old) also sits oddly with use being concentrated in states without floors.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Lilly filed the BLA in Jan 2029 on a phase 2b/3 trial showing about half the lean-mass loss with tirzepatide and similar total weight loss.
least_plausible_claims.why: Driver fidelity and magnitude: the parent lists bimagrumab-type adjuncts as phase 2/3 and unapproved. Approval 13 months after filing, on a DXA surrogate with no fracture data, is at the edge of the approval rules. It also rests on a phase 2/3 programme the parent never took to filing.

rationale.badness: Access broadens: Medicare covers about 15.5M users, the $50 copay and $245 lock apply, and the income gap narrows. Adherence conditioning is softened by the Illinois and California bans and the holiday allowances. New losers are older users on a doubled base with the unresolved hip-fracture HR of ~1.3, long-term users facing the 'lock-in' regain signal, and adolescents in states without age floors. Harms are measured and discussed openly, so this is a harder society with new risks but not a structurally hidden one.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Under federal mental-health parity, plans that dropped weight coverage must still cover AUD indications
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: parity law requires comparable limits on MH/SUD benefits. It does not force a plan to cover a specific drug for a newly approved indication, so the 'coverage backdoor' is a doubtful legal chain that the whole alcohol-and-employer story relies on.

least_plausible_claims.quote: A Danish national registry study linked to Kaiser Permanente data (Mar 2030, n≈38k who stopped after ≥5 years of continuous semaglutide use)
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism/magnitude: a cohort with 18 months of post-stopping follow-up published in Mar 2030 needs ≥5 years of continuous use ending by about Sep 2028, so starts by 2023. A cohort that size from Denmark plus one US insurer is hard to credit, and the ~115% regain and hypothalamic-adaptation story is asserted rather than built up.

rationale.badness: Access broadened through Medicare and Medicaid, so inequality narrows at the bottom, and AUD treatment and fewer drinkers are real benefits. Harms are named and measured (DSC, interim postmarketing data), so epistemic harm is modest. This is a recognisably harder society with new losers, not a structural nightmare.

Mechanism: opt-in states roughly triple from about 9 in 2028 (14 minus 5 dropouts) to 27, even though the starting world says Medicaid budgets were under pressure. The candidate gives no reason states would take on a ~$6B state share, because the Act's $245 rate and 'regular match' is not shown to differ from what was already on offer.
